subject: Outbound control policy and static egress IPs for private endpoints
messages:
From: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: EdgeGuard Solutions <ops@edgeguard.io>
Date: 2026-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: static outbound IPs for private deployment

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our onboarding for the Redwood Private deployment, our networking team needs a small list of stable outbound IPs (or a CIDR block) that our firewalls can accept for egress to external SaaS (license servers, telemetry endpoints, and your control plane callbacks). Requirements from our side:

- A concise list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses or ranges we can paste into the firewall (we run Palo Alto).
- Ports: ideally only 443 (we will block other ports unless you specify otherwise).
- A short description of failover behavior if you rotate IPs (how much lead time; do you support client-side allowlist updates?).
- Any TLS cert pinning or SNI requirements for downstream inspection.
- A contact for emergency IP changes (24/7).

Can EdgeGuard provide the official egress block and an ops contact? We need this in the next 48 hours to progress the environment build.

— Priya N., Acme Health Security
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, EdgeGuard Solutions <ops@edgeguard.io>
Date: 2026-04-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: static outbound IPs for private deployment

Priya —

Thanks, and great to meet you via email. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a stable set of egress IPs for Redwood Private (VPC/private control plane callbacks and optional edge-proxy egress). We typically support two modes:

1) Static IP blocks (recommended for regulated customers): a small set of /32 / /128 addresses we promise not to rotate without 7 days notice and a documented migration window.
2) Proxy egress through customer-managed NAT/Gateway: Redwood routes outbound through a customer-controlled egress point you own — this gives you full control, but requires config on your side.

Questions for our ops team (cc-ing Neha and Dev):
- Priya: do you need separate egress for telemetry/metrics vs control-plane callbacks, or can they share the same allowlist? The typical customer combines them (one outbound policy) but some customers segment telemetry.
- What firewall vendor/version are you on (you mentioned Palo Alto) and do you use TLS inspection (terminating client TLS) or pass-through?

Neha/Dev — Ive attached a working draft of our public egress list and a sample firewall rule that Acme can paste. Can you confirm the blackout/rotation SLA and emergency contact?

Next steps: Ill follow up with a concise CSV of IPs and a short ops runbook.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, EdgeGuard Solutions <ops@edgeguard.io>
Date: 2026-04-07T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: static outbound IPs for private deployment

Hi all —

Thanks for the context. Attached are three artifacts: (1) egress-ip-blocks.csv (canonical list of IPv4/IPv6 blocks we use for Redwood Private control-plane callbacks and hosted telemetry endpoints), (2) firewall-sample.conf (paloalto-friendly sample rule), and (3) redwood-edge-proxy-arch.drawio (high-level diagram showing supported egress topologies).

Operational notes (summary):
- Default ports: 443 (TLS) only. We do not require any other outbound ports for core functionality. If you enable log-forwarding to third-party collectors we may ask for additional TCP 443 endpoints.
- IP stability: for the Static IP Blocks mode we commit to 7 calendar days notice before removing or reassigning any published /32s. Emergency rotations (rare) will be emailed and we will attempt live websocket/phone coordination.
- IP Publication: we publish the canonical list in an internal CDN-backed CSV (link below); you can pull it programmatically from our URL or we can provide a signed snapshot for audit.
- TLS: we recommend pass-through TLS. If Acme requires TLS inspection, we recommend allowing SNI-based allowlist for control-plane endpoints and whitelisting our root domain patterns (control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai). Avoid cert pinning on your side for our control callbacks unless you have a pinned chain trust process — rotating certs will otherwise break connectivity.
- DNS/Egress policies: If your firewalls support FQDN-object rules, allow control.redwood.ai and telemetry.redwood.ai in addition to the static IPs; for strict offline environments rely on the CSV IPs only.

Emergency contact and SLA: on-call ops: ops@edgeguard.io (EdgeGuard) — they handle immediate NAT/egress issues; Redwood engineering escalation: infra-sre@redwood.ai (pager). We will also provide a short phone roster in the signed runbook.

Attachments referenced: egress-ip-blocks.csv, firewall-sample.conf, redwood-edge-proxy-arch.drawio

- Neha Kapoor
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Priya N. <security@acmehealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, EdgeGuard Solutions <ops@edgeguard.io>
Date: 2026-04-08T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: static outbound IPs for private deployment

Marcus / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. We validated the CSV against our firewall and everything looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we close the ticket: 

1) Can you confirm whether telemetry calls (metrics/traces) will ever originate from a different set of IPs than control-plane callbacks? We prefer a single allowlist to reduce rule churn.
2) For cert rotation: is there an automated notification feed (webhook or signed-URL) we can subscribe to that indicates planned certificate or IP changes?
3) EdgeGuard: can you confirm you'll be the 24/7 escalation contact for emergency IP swaps? Please provide a phone number we can add to our on-call playbook.

If those three items are answered we can finalize and enable the policy in our staging firewall tomorrow.

— Priya
Acme Health Security
